recommendations.regimenLabel: RAAS blockade + diuresis + statin (with cause-specific immunosuppression)
steps: Quantify proteinuria; renal biopsy in adults to define the lesion (guides specific therapy).
Reduce proteinuria with ACEi/ARB; manage oedema with salt restriction + loop diuretics (cautious).
Statin for hyperlipidaemia; consider VTE prophylaxis (high thrombotic risk, esp. albumin <20-25 g/L).
Cause-specific immunosuppression (e.g. steroids for minimal change) per nephrology.
Treat secondary causes (diabetes, amyloid, drugs, infection); vaccination.

drugRefs.why: Reduces intraglomerular pressure and proteinuria; an ARB is an alternative if ACEi not tolerated. Monitor U&E/potassium.

drugRefs.dose: 40 mg (titrate to response; higher doses often needed)
drugRefs.why: Controls oedema alongside salt restriction; use cautiously to avoid intravascular depletion/AKI.
Treats the secondary hyperlipidaemia of nephrotic syndrome.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Glomerular Diseases

UpToDate — Overview of the Management of Nephrotic Syndrome in Adults

drugRefs.why: Nephrotic syndrome is strongly prothrombotic, especially when serum albumin is <20-25 g/L; consider prophylactic anticoagulation.
Cause-specific immunosuppression example (minimal change disease); the specific regimen depends on the biopsy diagnosis and is directed by nephrology.

decision.label: ACEi/ARB + diuretics + statin; nephrology for biopsy-directed therapy

confirm: Heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminaemia, oedema ± hyperlipidaemia. Identify primary vs secondary cause; biopsy in adults.
